rationale: The exact entry's core unifies the printed references under the curse-ground crop of Genesis 3:18 as the same fruitless growth that the OT already identifies with divided-heart riches and that Jesus grades as cares/riches choking the word, while the bramble and Belial-thorn texts supply the false-shadow and end-in-fire mechanics. This accounts for the cross-text pattern and the Teacher's own key more tightly than a looser polyvalent-curse reading of the same verses. Secondary clauses in the entry are directly carried by the cited texts and require no extra steps.
book_core_identification: Thorns/brambles/briers are the curse-ground's own fruitless growth (Gen 3:18), identified as worldly care and deceitful riches that choke the word
chapter_only_objections: Broader claim that every kingdom-parable element is uniformly pre-decoded solely from OT patterns with perfect Teacher-key matches
Extension of the same method to mustard, leaven, treasure, pearl, net, and feeding sign
Assertion that the entire symbolic language of Scripture is this dense and that modern tools uniquely unlock sealed knowledge
strongest_counter_interpretation: Thorns, thistles, briers and the bramble primarily and generally symbolize the curse on the ground after the Fall together with its outworkings in unfruitfulness, hardship, desolation and divine judgment; the cares/riches sense is only the local application inside the Sower, the false-shade/fire sense is local to Jotham's fable, and the Belial/burning sense is local to the worthless, so the entry over-unifies distinct contextual uses under one gloss.
counter_core_identification: General symbol of the post-Fall curse and its consequences (unfruitfulness, judgment, obstruction)
material_core_denial: Denies that worldly care and deceitful riches constitute the governing identification of the curse-ground crop across the cited cluster, treating that sense as merely one local reading among others
counter_case: Genesis 3:18 introduces thorns as part of the ground's curse without naming cares or riches
Hebrews 6:8 and the prophetic brier texts speak of rejected/desolate land under judgment without requiring the Sower's cares gloss
Judges 9:15 and 2 Samuel 23:6-7 portray worthless/hostile agents that burn, which can be read as judgment imagery rather than specifically 'deceitful riches'
Mainstream reading already recognizes polyvalence and therefore needs no single forced synthesis
book_explanatory_advantages: Derives the Sower's thorns directly from the curse-crop + Hosea's divided-heart riches + Isaiah's brier-men (monopoly and pleasure), so Matt 13:22 is the OT pattern graded, not a new invention
Places the bramble's offered shadow and the fire that comes out of it, plus the Belial-thorns burned on the spot, as natural extensions of the same fruitless, non-protective, end-in-fire crop
Makes the five printed references mutually reinforcing witnesses rather than unrelated local metaphors
Explains why the same plants appear both as what chokes fruit and as what is itself burned
counter_explanatory_advantages: Preserves ordinary contextual flexibility without requiring every thorn text to carry cares/riches
Aligns with the broad Christian consensus that Genesis 3 supplies the root image while later texts apply it variously
decisive_sources: Genesis 3:17-19 (curse-crop in the field of anxious toil)
Hosea 10:1-8 and Isaiah 5:6-12 (thorn/thistle and briers as riches/pleasures that divide the heart and replace fruit)
Matthew 13:22 (Teacher's key matching the derived sense)
Judges 9:15 (false shadow + fire from the bramble)
2 Samuel 23:6-7 and Hebrews 6:8 (thorns thrust away and burned)
